written.myAnswer: Data visualization presents information visually, often using charts and graphs. It helps people understand complex data by making comparisons and patterns easier to see.

First decide what information the survey should find out. Prepare questions about students’ favourite extracurricular activities and choose which students to ask. Collect their responses, organize and check the data, analyse the results, and present the findings clearly, for example with a bar chart.

Data visualization represents data visually using charts, graphs, or other displays, helping people understand complex information and notice patterns. For example, a bar chart can compare students’ sports preferences, while a line graph can show how a quantity changes over time.

Visualization makes data easier to understand, helps reveal patterns and comparisons, and communicates findings clearly. Businesses and decision-makers can use charts, graphs, and dashboards to understand insights and make informed decisions.

Nominal data consists of categories with no natural order, such as favourite sports; a bar chart can compare their counts. Ordinal data consists of categories with a meaningful order, such as satisfaction ratings; an ordered bar chart can display them. Discrete data consists of separate countable values, such as the number of siblings; a dot plot or bar chart can show their frequencies. Continuous data can take any measured value within a range, such as height; a histogram can show its distribution.
